However, ION did not have continuous analysis on the inlet flue gas and thus could not determine the source of these emissions. For the last month of testing with an aged solvent, emissions of acetaldehyde, the only detected Hazardous Air Pollutant (HAP), were generally below 2 to 3 ppbv with the highest reading around 7 ppbv. Other VOC emissions associated with the solvent were generally below 1 ppbv with the highest reading around 3 ppbv. These results demonstrate the excellent emissions performance that can be achieved with ICE-31® and NGCC flue gas in an ION-designed pilot facility. Ammonia emissions measured by the PTR-TOF were approximately 1 ppmv, with dips down to approximately 0.8 ppmv and spikes up to approximately 10 ppmv. 9.3.6 CO Product Analysis 2 ION sampled the CO product stream five separate times using sample kits rented from Airborne 2 Labs International. The kits consist of a sample system and bag that were shipped to Airborne Labs for analysis. The sample bag was purged at least three times before taking the actual sample. There was no NO or SO detected in any of the samples above the detection limit (0.5 ppmv).
